channel.title: Highball
channel.description: Run Windows games on Apple Silicon.

item.title: Highball 0.6.3
item.description: Fixes the crash some of you hit right after a launcher or game closed (the 'Highball quit unexpectedly' dialog, most common on M4 and M5 Macs) — root-caused from a reader's crash report. Also: dropping an unsupported file on a bottle now tells you which file types work instead of doing nothing.

item.title: Highball 0.6.2
item.description: You can now run any Windows .exe or .msi from the GUI without knowing the secret: a 'Run a Windows program…' button lives under the launchers (also File menu, ⌘O), opening the same run-or-pin flow as drag-and-drop — which still works, and is now labeled so you can actually find it.

item.title: Highball 0.6.1
item.description: New Dependencies section in bottle settings: one-click install of the Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtimes (the 'Microsoft Visual C++ runtime error' fix many games need), with install-state tracking. More runtimes will follow as they're verified on the engine.

item.title: Highball 0.6.0
item.description: Three additions from your launch-week feedback: a Report a Problem button that opens a pre-filled GitHub issue with your system info and latest log; Steam's slow first update now shows its progress inline and auto-recovers from its known mid-update crash; and bottles can be duplicated (safe backups) and repaired from the sidebar's right-click menu.

item.title: Highball 0.5.7
item.description: New: Retina mode — a per-bottle toggle in Settings for crisp text and UI at your display's native resolution (with a DPI bump so nothing goes microscopic). Off by default: native rendering is heavier, so pair it with the frame rate cap for demanding games.

item.title: Highball 0.5.6
item.description: Fixes a crash at launch when a bottle folder had been copied or duplicated in Finder — the copy now just appears as its own working bottle. If Highball was crashing on open for you, this is the fix.

item.title: Highball 0.5.5
item.description: Games can now use your microphone: macOS will show the standard permission prompt the first time a game or app in a bottle asks for it. Previously the app was missing the required declarations, so voice chat got silently denied with no prompt.

item.title: Highball 0.5.4
item.description: Engine installs now show live download progress (per-component MB counts) instead of a blank sheet, and a stalled connection fails with a clear error after 60 seconds instead of hanging forever. Also: CLI quickstart fixes for source builds (recipe lookup guidance, bare program names route through Wine).

item.title: Highball 0.5.3
item.description: Quitting Highball now offers to stop all Windows processes (or deliberately leave a game running) instead of silently stranding them — and the app menu gains Stop All Windows Processes for cleanup after a crash.

item.title: Highball 0.5.2
item.description: Bottle names are now validated before creation: names with characters Windows forbids in paths (\ / : * ? " < > |) silently broke the Wine prefix (wineboot exit 53). The New Bottle sheet now explains the problem inline. Fixes #12.

item.title: Highball 0.5.1
item.description: Hotfix: creating your first bottle failed on fresh installs (the app pointed Wine's working directory at a folder that only exists after first boot). If 0.5.0 wouldn't make a bottle for you — this is the fix, and it'll arrive via Check for Updates too.

item.title: Highball 0.5.0
item.description: The design release. Highball now looks like what it is — a game launcher: full-bleed artwork cards with verdicts on the art and play-on-hover, one launcher row where installed means Open and missing means Install, Highball's amber through the whole shell instead of system blue, and settings tucked into a toolbar sheet where they belong. Same engine, same database, entirely different feel.

item.title: Highball 0.4.1
item.description: Design pass: branded sidebar, amber bottle header, launcher tiles with icons, humanized engine names, game-card hover states, empty states, and the redesigned compatibility database site with 12,491 predictions. Plus the automated verification harness from 0.4.0, now with display-wake fixed.

item.title: Highball 0.4.0
item.description: The database learns to feed itself: automated verification harness (highball verify — tests your installed games under every renderer, detects crashes and black screens, records provenance-complete verdicts; anti-cheat titles skipped by design), 12,491 machine-derived Mac predictions on the database site, Mac-aware anti-cheat map for 1,166 titles, UI polish (game-card hover, humanized engine names, empty states), and a landing page at gauthierpiarrette.github.io/highball.

item.title: Highball 0.3.1
item.description: Notarized build with automatic updates. macOS opens it without any right-click ritual, and this is the last version you'll ever download by hand — updates arrive in-app via Sparkle. Includes everything from 0.3.0: +42% game frame rate via msync, DXVK async, frame-rate caps, game library with compatibility verdicts, French UI.
